title: Who makes the iPhone's brain? #iphone
yt:

title: The iPhone motherboard is a lasagna #iphone
yt:
The iPhone's motherboard isn't one board: it's two, stacked like a lasagna. Apple started this with the iPhone X in 2017 to save about 30% of the space. On the iPhone 18 Pro, the storage chip now hides inside the sandwich.

Full teardown: What's inside an iPhone? (on the channel)

ig:

title: How Face ID sees you in the dark #iphone
yt:
How does Face ID work in the dark? A tiny projector throws more than 30,000 invisible infrared dots on your face, and an infrared camera builds a 3D map. Most Android phones use the selfie camera instead: in a Which? test, 133 of 208 phones were unlocked with a printed photo.

yt:

title: Why does the iPhone camera have blades? #iphone
yt:
The iPhone 18 Pro main camera has a variable aperture: six tiny blades that open and close like your pupil, moved by electromagnets. Wide open, about seven times more light. Android did it first: the Galaxy S9 had two apertures in 2018.

title: There's water inside your iPhone #iphone
yt:
How do you cool a phone with no fan? With water. Since the iPhone 17 Pro, a vapor chamber with a little pure water sealed inside moves heat away from the chip. On the iPhone 18 Pro it's three times bigger. Gaming Android phones had one back in 2018.

Full teardown: What's inside an iPhone? (on the channel)

ig:
There's water inside your iPhone 💧

title: What are an iPhone's parts really worth? #iphone
yt:
